name: Struve Geodetic Arc
countries: Latvia, Norway, Sweden, Belarus, Estonia, Finland, Ukraine, Lithuania, Republic of Moldova, Russian Federation
description: The Struve Arc is a chain of survey points running 2,820 km from Hammerfest in Arctic Norway to the Black Sea, crossing ten countries. Between 1816 and 1855, astronomer Friedrich Struve used it to measure a long stretch of the Earth's curve and work out the planet's size and shape. Today you can visit 34 surviving stations, marked by rock-drilled holes, iron crosses, cairns and stone obelisks.
